newsitem.title: USA: US Rubin--productivity tempering wage inflation.
newsitem.headline: US Rubin--productivity tempering wage inflation.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said recent wage gains have been offset by increasing productivity, which minimizes their inflationary threat.
"The danger comes when wages rise too much in excess of productivity and I do not see that happening," said Rubin in an interview with CNN television.
While noting that inflation always bears a close watch, Rubin added that the U.S. economy currently has very low inflation.

"All my experience over the 26 years I spent on Wall Street suggests to me that you always have to be watchful about inflation. But I must say, I don't see evidence of inflation in anything that I see," Rubin said.
Rubin stressed the U.S. economy's strong recent performance, with unemployment at a 24-year low, tame inflation and low interest rates.
"Economic conditions in this country are very strong and they've been strong for quite some time now," he added.
Rubin denied that U.S. officials will use the shining U.S. economic performance to cajole their partners in the Group of Seven to emulate U.S. policies at this weekend's summit.
But the Treasury secretary then urged European nations plagued by double-digit unemployment rates to reform their labor and capital markets in an effort to stimulate economic growth.
"Flexibility in labor and capital markets is critical to economic success in a modern economy," he added.
